newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end flat as U.S. stocks start higher.
newsitem.headline: German shares end flat as U.S. stocks start higher.

text.p: German blue-chip shares ended the day mostly steady on Friday, managing a late recovery from earlier losses in post-bourse trade after Wall Street started its Friday session higher.

The IBIS-DAX index of electronic trade finished a bare 0.60 points lower at 3,361.20 following the earlier 1.15 percent fall in the DAX-30 index to 3,344.39 points, with export-driven car and chemical shares suffering losses.
Cash market orders had been thin with activity dominated by options dealers due to an expiry deadline for options on the DAX index and some constituents.
The bulk of the decline was a catch-up with losses that occured in post-bourse trade on Thursday after comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer against a weak mark that undermined the dollar.
But despite the late recovery with Wall Street, dealers were wary of ascribing a more positive long-term trend to the market.
"Nobody is trusting the gains on Wall Street anymore," said one trader, noting widespread expectations of a further U.S. Federal Reserve interest rate increase in May.
He added that the German market might as a result underperform any new gains made among U.S. shares.

Within the DAX, drugs and chemicals group Hoechst saw among the highest volumes of the day, continuing to ease 15 pfennigs in reaction to a poorly-received presentation to British institutionals on Thursday.
Dealers said however that earlier market rumours the group would issue a profit warning were now being discounted.
Siemens AG rose strongly in post-bourse trade as dealers said the market was expecting good results from the electrical and engineering group when it publishes first-half figures next Wednesday.
Siemens shares, which were largely flat in bourse trade, gained 1.21 marks to 89.13 by the end of electronic dealings.

In the auto sector, Daimler-Benz AG lost 1.95 marks to 130.40 and BMW AG was down 18.0 marks at 1,389.0 marks. Dealers said the drop was more of a correction than the start of a trend, adding there was a still a degree of bullishness surrounding the stocks.
